notes.content:
Found while validating gh-79, but PRE-EXISTING and NOT caused by the annotation port.

draw_path.rs:190 stroke_to_polygons has a standing TODO: no true miter/round/bevel joins
and no end caps at all. It emits a quad per segment plus an axis-aligned SQUARE bridging
interior vertices; segment ends get butt caps regardless of the content stream's J/j.

Measured on ~/Desktop/test-annotation.pdf page 1 at 150dpi, 25 ink strokes:
  poppler       10821 blue px
  kopitiam-pdf   9286 blue px   (86%)
The synthesised ink appearance explicitly emits '1 J 1 j' (round caps/joins) exactly as
MuPDF does -- pdf-appearance.c:1050 -- and annot_appearance.rs ports that faithfully. Our
rasterizer just ignores it. Round caps add a half-disc at each of 50 stroke ends, which
accounts for most of the shortfall.

Also means the single-point ink dot case (a zero-length 'l' relying on round caps to paint
at all) will render as nothing rather than a dot. Upstream: fz_flatten_stroke_path.

title: kopitiam-pdf: stroker ignores line caps/joins (1 J / 1 j) -- strokes render ~14% light
